activity: Read a story aloud to baby
evidence_summary: Fetus hears from ~19-24 wk; newborns recognise passages read aloud before birth. No evidence it raises IQ.

activity: Talk to baby / narrate your day
evidence_summary: Mother's voice is the most prominent sound in the womb; term fetuses respond differently to it.
Voice and melody exposure; newborn neural memory for prenatally heard melody/speech; mother's singing may aid bonding.
key_sources: Partanen et al. 2013 (PNAS); Persico et al. 2017

activity: Same story, same song ritual (from week 30)
evidence_summary: Repeated exposure produces familiarity/recognition after birth.
Meta-analyses: small-moderate reduction in maternal anxiety; no effect on general stress.
key_sources: Corbijn van Willenswaard 2017; Lin et al. 2019
safety_note: Comfortable volume; never headphones on the belly.

evidence_summary: Pilot fMRI showed limbic deactivation; slow-exhale breathing linked to parasympathetic activity.
key_sources: Kalyani et al. 2011; Bernardi et al. 2001
safety_note: Soft voice; no breath-holding; stop if dizzy.

evidence_summary: Mantra recitation slows breathing; mantra meditation small benefits (weak studies). Heritage: Rigveda 3.62.10.
safety_note: Some traditions require initiation; respect family custom.

activity: Shanti mantra (Saha navavatu / Asato ma / Purnamadah)
evidence_summary: As for mantra meditation; meaning-centred reflection.
key_sources: Lynch et al. 2018; Taittiriya Up. 2.1; BU 1.3.28; BU 5.1.1
secular_alternative: Read a calming verse or prayer of your own faith

evidence_summary: Heritage lullaby of wisdom (Markandeya Purana tradition). Singing itself is voice exposure (see M03).
Voice + language melody exposure; newborns attuned to native-language prosody.
key_sources: Partanen et al. 2013; Moon et al. 2013 (Acta Paediatrica)

evidence_summary: Reading aloud = voice exposure (see M01); story content is cultural.

activity: Shloka of the week: read the meaning and reflect
evidence_summary: Contemplative reading; meaning-focused reflection.
key_sources: Yoga Sutras; Bhagavad Gita; Upanishads (see notes §2.8)
secular_alternative: Quote of the week from any wisdom tradition

evidence_summary: Music/nature sound listening reduces anxiety in small trials.
safety_note: Comfortable volume.

evidence_summary: Voice exposure; supports parental mentalising & attachment.
Slow breathing reduces physiological arousal; standard antenatal relaxation skill.
key_sources: ACOG CO 804; Zaccaro et al. 2018 (Front Hum Neurosci)
safety_note: Stop if dizzy or breathless. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Slow yogic breathing; parasympathetic shift in small studies.
safety_note: No breath-holding; slow, gentle; skip with blocked nose. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Very-low-quality studies show parasympathetic effects; humming raises nasal nitric oxide.
safety_note: No ear pressing if uncomfortable; no breath-holding; stop if dizzy. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Traditional cooling breath; minimal evidence; low risk.
safety_note: Skip if you have asthma, a cold, low BP or sensitive teeth; no retention. Check with your doctor first.
secular_alternative: Slow nose breathing with a cool cloth

evidence_summary: WHO/ACOG: moderate activity safe and beneficial; lowers GDM, pre-eclampsia risk.
safety_note: Talk test; avoid heat; stop with warning signs. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Antenatal PFMT reduces urinary incontinence late pregnancy & postpartum.
safety_note: Don't do while urinating; breathe normally. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Gentle stretching within prenatal activity guidance.
safety_note: Slow; no forcing; stop if pain. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Included in safe postures studied in 3rd trimester; eases back discomfort.
key_sources: Polis et al. 2015; Corrigan et al. 2022
safety_note: Keep back neutral to gentle; no deep sagging. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Gentle hip opener common in prenatal yoga programmes.
safety_note: Sit on a cushion; no bouncing; stop with pelvic (SPD) pain. Check with your doctor first.

activity: Mountain pose with gentle side stretch (Tadasana / Tiryaka)
evidence_summary: Standing posture & gentle stretch; studied safe postures.
safety_note: Feet hip-width; hold a chair if unsteady. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Common prenatal back-care exercise.
safety_note: Gentle range; stop if pain. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Avoids supine position after 1st trimester; relaxation reduces perceived stress.
safety_note: Pillow between knees; no flat-on-back after 1st trimester. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Circulation & comfort; low risk.
safety_note: Gentle; report one-sided calf pain/swelling at once. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Balance practice; fall risk managed with wall support.
safety_note: Always beside a wall or chair; skip in 3rd trimester if unsteady. Check with your doctor first.

activity: Modified warrior II (Virabhadrasana II), short hold
evidence_summary: Among postures studied as well tolerated.
safety_note: Short stance; chair nearby; no strain. Check with your doctor first.

activity: Gentle open seated twist (away from belly)
evidence_summary: Gentle mobility; closed/deep twists avoided.
key_sources: Prenatal yoga practice consensus; ACOG CO 804
safety_note: Twist from upper back only, open away from belly; skip if uncomfortable. Check with your doctor first.

activity: Guided relaxation / yoga nidra (side-lying or propped)
evidence_summary: Guided relaxation in integrated yoga RCT reduced perceived stress, raised HRV.
safety_note: Side-lying or propped; never flat on back after 1st trimester.

activity: Partner hand or foot massage (plain oil/lotion)
evidence_summary: Massage reduced anxiety/depressive symptoms in small trials.
safety_note: Gentle pressure; no strong essential oils; skip if calf is swollen/painful. Check with your doctor first.

evidence_summary: Expressive writing small wellbeing benefits; supports maternal-fetal attachment.
Gratitude interventions small positive effects (general populations).
Expressive writing; cognitive reframing.
safety_note: If low mood lasts 2+ weeks, talk to your doctor.

evidence_summary: Fetus hears external voices from mid-pregnancy; familiarity after birth.

activity: Partner task of the week (practical support)
evidence_summary: Social support protects maternal mental health.

activity: Record a voice message or lullaby for baby
evidence_summary: Keepsake and bonding; voice familiarity.
Cultural practice of ashirvad; social support.
Fetuses moved more in response to maternal abdominal touch.
safety_note: Gentle touch only.

activity: Reach out: call a friend / ask for help
evidence_summary: Social support reduces stress & depression risk.
Maternal-fetal attachment linked to postnatal bonding.
Structured mandala colouring reduced state anxiety vs free colouring (students).
Contemplative focus; heritage. Eyes soft, blink freely, no strain.
key_sources: Sri Vidya tradition; Hatha Yoga Pradipika (trataka) context
safety_note: Blink normally; stop if eyes water/strain; no candle-staring for long.
secular_alternative: Gaze at a flower or geometric pattern

evidence_summary: Heritage geometry (9 triangles, 43 sub-triangles); also structured colouring (see S01).
Threshold art of India; mindful repetitive drawing.

activity: Mudra with calm breath (Gyan, Dhyana, Anjali, Shuni, Prana; Apana only near term)
evidence_summary: Hand gestures from ritual/dance/meditation; therapeutic claims unproven; pleasant focus for breathing.
safety_note: Hands relaxed; no strain.
secular_alternative: Rest hands on belly or knees

evidence_summary: Brief mindfulness practice; mindfulness interventions show mixed but encouraging results in pregnancy.
Symbolic framework (Sat-cakra-nirupana 1577; Woodroffe 1919); used as emotional check-in, not anatomy.

activity: Pancha kosha check-in (body, breath, mind, wisdom, joy)
evidence_summary: Taittiriya Upanishad 2.1-2.5 framework, used as self-care checklist.
Guided imagery reduces anxiety in small studies.
Loving-kindness meditation increases positive emotion (general populations).
key_sources: Hofmann et al. 2011 (Clin Psychol Rev); Yoga Sutra 1.33
secular_alternative: Kind wishes for yourself, baby, family

evidence_summary: Creative activity; see S01.
Nature exposure & mindfulness; general wellbeing evidence.
safety_note: Avoid isolated/unsafe places at night.

activity: Folate foods (dal, rajma, palak, methi, oranges)
evidence_summary: Folate essential for neural tube; supplements prescribed by doctor.
safety_note: Take supplements only as your doctor prescribes.

activity: Iron foods + vitamin C pairing; tea/coffee away from meals
evidence_summary: Prevents anaemia; vitamin C enhances non-haem iron absorption.
Iodine essential for fetal brain/thyroid.
safety_note: Moderate salt if BP is high (doctor advice).

activity: Choline foods (eggs; soy, paneer, peanuts for vegetarians)
evidence_summary: Choline supports fetal brain development; small RCT shows faster infant processing at higher intake.
safety_note: Eggs fully cooked.

evidence_summary: Omega-3 LCPUFA reduces preterm birth; DHA for brain/retina.
safety_note: Avoid high-mercury fish; DHA supplement only if doctor advises.

evidence_summary: Increased protein needs in 2nd/3rd trimesters.
Bone development; calcium lowers pre-eclampsia risk where intake low.

activity: Water & fluids (8-10 glasses unless advised otherwise)
evidence_summary: Hydration, constipation, UTI prevention.
safety_note: Follow doctor advice if fluid restricted.

activity: Food safety: pasteurised milk, cooked eggs/meat, washed produce
evidence_summary: Prevents listeriosis, toxoplasmosis, salmonellosis.
ICMR-NIN recommends small frequent meals for nausea.
safety_note: Call doctor if you cannot keep fluids down.

activity: Mindful eating (one meal a day slowly, no screens)
evidence_summary: Mindful eating may help appetite awareness; limited pregnancy data.
Cultural/historical summary only; not dietary advice.
safety_note: Discuss any diet change with your doctor.

evidence_summary: Vegetarians at risk of B12 deficiency; important for neural development.
safety_note: Ask doctor about testing/supplements.

evidence_summary: Moderate caffeine not a major factor in miscarriage/preterm birth.
Flavours reach amniotic fluid; prenatal exposure increases acceptance at weaning.

activity: Morning calm routine (water, stretch, breath, intention)
evidence_summary: Combines B01, B07, S06; routine supports wellbeing.
safety_note: Components carry their own cautions.

evidence_summary: Sleep hygiene; side-sleeping from 28 wk lowers stillbirth risk.
safety_note: Go to sleep on your side from 28 weeks.

evidence_summary: Supine going-to-sleep position associated with ~2.3x late stillbirth risk.
safety_note: Don't worry if you wake on your back; turn to your side.

activity: Know your baby's movement pattern (kick awareness)
evidence_summary: Awareness of baby's own pattern; report reduced movement immediately; formal counts not evidence-based.
safety_note: If movements reduce or change, call your hospital now; don't use home Dopplers.

evidence_summary: Early recognition of perinatal depression/anxiety enables help.
safety_note: Low mood 2+ weeks or thoughts of self-harm: contact doctor / Tele-MANAS 14416.

evidence_summary: Self-monitoring supports healthy habits.
Antenatal care attendance (WHO: 8 contacts) improves outcomes.
Voice exposure; intergenerational support.

activity: Godh bharai / seemantham / valaikappu / sadh / dohale jevan planner
evidence_summary: Heritage celebrations rooted in simantonnayana (Ashvalayana GS 1.14); social support.
safety_note: Celebration only; no sex prediction games or rituals; keep mother rested.

evidence_summary: Belonging, heritage.

activity: Pumsavana reframed: 3rd-month blessing for a healthy child
evidence_summary: Historic rite expressed wish for a son; reframed as blessing for any child; sex selection illegal (PC&PNDT 1994).
safety_note: No herbs/nostril rite; no sex prediction.
secular_alternative: Family wishes for a healthy baby

evidence_summary: Naming heritage (namakarana).

activity: Hospital bag, birth preferences, newborn prep
evidence_summary: Preparation reduces anxiety; birth preparedness recommended by MoHFW.
